title: Independence of the Continuum Hypothesis
description: The Continuum Hypothesis is independent of ZFC set theory. Godel showed CH is consistent with ZFC; Cohen showed not-CH is also consistent.

meta.author: Godel (1940) and Cohen (1963)
originalContributions: Framework for ZFC models and relative consistency
meta.assumptions: 4 axiom declarations: L_exists (constructible universe L exists as ZFC model), L_satisfies_CH (L satisfies CH), forcing_extension_exists (Cohen forcing extension exists), forcing_violates_CH (forcing model violates CH). Previously 6 axioms; ch_implies_no_intermediate and no_intermediate_implies_ch are now proved from Mathlib cardinal arithmetic.

overview.historicalContext: Cantor first posed the Continuum Hypothesis in his 1878 paper *Ein Beitrag zur Mannigfaltigkeitslehre*, conjecturing that $2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_1$ after proving the reals are uncountable (1873). Hilbert placed it as Problem #1 in his famous 1900 Paris address, calling it the most important open problem in mathematics. After decades of failed attempts, Gödel resolved half the question in 1940 by constructing the *Constructible Universe* L—a minimal model of ZFC in which CH holds—proving Con(ZFC) → Con(ZFC+CH). Cohen revolutionised logic in 1963 by inventing *forcing*, a general method for extending set-theoretic models, and used it to produce models where CH fails (Con(ZFC) → Con(ZFC+¬CH)). Cohen received the Fields Medal in 1966, the only one awarded for work in logic. Together, Gödel and Cohen showed CH is *independent* of ZFC—Hilbert's first problem was answered, but not by deciding its truth.
overview.problemStatement:
**Continuum Hypothesis**: There is no set with cardinality strictly between aleph_0 (countable infinity) and 2^(aleph_0) (the continuum).

Equivalently: |R| = aleph_1.

**Independence**: CH can neither be proved nor disproved from ZFC axioms.
overview.text: The Continuum Hypothesis is independent of ZFC set theory. Godel showed CH is consistent with ZFC; Cohen showed not-CH is also consistent.
overview.proofStrategy: Model-theoretic: Godel's constructible universe L is a model of ZFC where CH holds. Cohen's forcing constructs a model where CH fails. Since both are consistent with ZFC, CH is independent.
keyInsights: The constructible universe L satisfies V = L and implies GCH
Forcing allows construction of models with almost any cardinal arithmetic
Independence means ZFC doesn't determine the size of the continuum
New axioms (large cardinals, forcing axioms) may decide CH
Cohen's forcing technique, invented for this problem, became the central tool of modern set theory and enabled hundreds of subsequent independence results

sections.title: Module Header and Setup
sections.summary: Lean 4 imports, ZFC axiom framework, and problem description for the independence of CH.
sections.mathContext: The Continuum Hypothesis: $2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_1$, equivalently $|\mathbb{R}| = \aleph_1$. Hilbert's first problem (1900). The formalization uses Mathlib's `Cardinal` type and `Cardinal.aleph` for the aleph hierarchy.

sections.title: Cardinals and the Continuum
sections.summary: Continuum, aleph-one, and the CH statement.
sections.mathContext: The continuum $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0} = |\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})| = |\mathbb{R}|$. Cantor's theorem: $|S| < |\mathcal{P}(S)|$, so $\aleph_0 < 2^{\aleph_0}$. CH asserts there is no cardinal $\kappa$ with $\aleph_0 < \kappa < 2^{\aleph_0}$, i.e., the first uncountable cardinal $\aleph_1$ equals the continuum.

sections.title: Godel's Constructible Universe
sections.summary: The inner model L where CH holds.
sections.mathContext: Gödel's constructible universe $L = \bigcup_{\alpha \in \text{Ord}} L_\alpha$, built by iterating definable power sets: $L_0 = \emptyset$, $L_{\alpha+1} = \text{Def}(L_\alpha)$, $L_\lambda = \bigcup_{\alpha < \lambda} L_\alpha$ for limit $\lambda$. $L$ is the minimal inner model of ZFC, and $L \models \text{CH}$ because the definability constraint restricts $\mathcal{P}(\omega) \cap L$ to $\aleph_1$-many sets.

sections.title: Cohen's Forcing
sections.mathContext: Cohen forcing adds $\aleph_2$-many new subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ to a ground model $M$, producing $M[G]$ where $2^{\aleph_0} \geq \aleph_2 > \aleph_1$, violating CH. The forcing poset is $\text{Fn}(\aleph_2 \times \omega, 2)$ — finite partial functions from $\aleph_2 \times \omega$ to $\{0,1\}$. Each generic filter $G$ encodes $\aleph_2$-many distinct reals.

sections.title: The Independence Theorem
sections.summary: Main result: CH is independent of ZFC.
sections.mathContext: $\text{Con}(\text{ZFC}) \Rightarrow \text{Con}(\text{ZFC} + \text{CH})$ (Gödel, 1940) and $\text{Con}(\text{ZFC}) \Rightarrow \text{Con}(\text{ZFC} + \neg\text{CH})$ (Cohen, 1963). Therefore CH is independent of ZFC: it can be neither proved nor refuted from the standard axioms. This resolved Hilbert's first problem — but not by deciding CH's truth value.

conclusion.summary: The independence of CH resolved Hilbert's first problem, but not in the way expected. It revealed fundamental limitations of ZFC and opened new research directions in set theory, including forcing axioms and the set-theoretic multiverse.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: The resolution has philosophical implications for mathematical truth and the nature of infinity.

It also led to extensive research on large cardinals, inner models, and forcing axioms.
openQuestions: Should we adopt axioms that decide CH?
What is the 'true' size of the continuum?
Does the set-theoretic multiverse perspective resolve the question?

crossReferences.description: Cantor's diagonal argument proves |ℕ| < |ℝ|, the starting point for CH. The continuum hypothesis asks whether any cardinality lies strictly between — proved independent by Gödel (1940) and Cohen (1963)
Cantor's theorem |S| < |P(S)| gives |ℕ| < |P(ℕ)| = |ℝ|. CH asserts this is the NEXT cardinal: ℵ₁ = 2^ℵ₀. The generalized CH (GCH) extends this to all infinite cardinals

Both reveal fundamental limitations of formal systems: Gödel's incompleteness shows ZFC cannot prove all arithmetic truths, and CH's independence shows ZFC cannot decide all set-theoretic questions. Gödel's constructible universe L (used in the consistency proof) connects both results

Both are undecidability results in their respective domains: the halting problem shows no algorithm decides all computation questions, CH's independence shows no ZFC proof decides the continuum's cardinality
Schröder-Bernstein establishes cardinality equality from mutual injections. CH concerns the question of which cardinalities exist between ℵ₀ and 2^ℵ₀ — a question Schröder-Bernstein cannot answer

The countability of $\mathbb{Q}$ ($|\mathbb{Q}| = \aleph_0$) establishes the lower bound: $\mathbb{Q}$ has the same cardinality as $\mathbb{N}$. CH asks whether $2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_1$, i.e., whether $\mathbb{R}$ is the next cardinality above countable sets like $\mathbb{Q}$.

Both are landmark independence results: CH is independent of ZFC (Gödel 1940, Cohen 1963), the parallel postulate is independent of the other Euclidean axioms (Lobachevsky, Bolyai 1830s). Both spawned new mathematical universes — non-Euclidean geometry and forcing extensions of set theory.

Erdős Problem #70 concerns partition calculus for the continuum: $2^{\aleph_0} \to (\aleph_1)^2_2$. The truth value depends on CH — under CH, $2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_1$ and the partition relation fails; under $\neg$CH, it may hold.
Explores the Continuum Hypothesis in depth: whether cardinalities exist between $|\mathbb{N}|$ and $|\mathbb{R}|$, examining Gödel's constructible universe $L$ and Cohen's forcing.
